business_scope.primary_industry_name: Eco-Friendly Beechwood Turning of Non-Toxic Sensory Toddler Toys

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax differentiation within the scope)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romanistic tradition, with separate administrative law governed by the Conseil d'État)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 26 November 2013; applicable from 1 January 2015)
Agreement between France and China on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (signed 26 November 2007; in force since 17 August 2010)
France–United States Double Taxation Convention (1967, as amended by the 2006 and 2009 Protocols)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Articles 49 and 63 (freedom of establishment and free movement of capital)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI), ratified by France

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 to R.561-60 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), as amended by Ordinance No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 and Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 July 2017, transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AML Directive 4) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AML Directive 5); beneficial-owner filing obligations under Articles L.123-22 and R.123-208 to R.123-223 of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce); implementation framework for Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (single EU AML rulebook); register operated administratively by INPI and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — The French registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) is accessible to French supervisory authorities, financial intelligence (Tracfin), tax and customs authorities, and AML/CFT obliged entities; general public access was restricted following the Court of Justice of the European Union rulings of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 WM and C-601/20 Sovim), and access is granted only upon demonstration of a legitimate interest.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / current registration extract of each foreign corporate UBO or direct shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (PRC) / equivalent foreign company registry (e.g., US Secretary of State, Companies House, RCS of origin)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) — PRC-issued documents are subject to apostille only since the PRC's accession in force on 7 November 2023; EU-origin public documents are exempt under Regulation (EU) 2016/1191; non-Hague jurisdictions require French consular legalization. Where the document is not in French, a sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) is additionally mandatory.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (attestation de conformité / non-inscription en procédure collective) of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry or competent authority of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; EU-origin certificates exempt under Regulation (EU) 2016/1191; otherwise French consular legalization plus sworn French translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of valid passport/ID of each natural-person UBO shareholder and of the proposed gérant (manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or public notary office of the country of issuance of the identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or French consular legalization for non-Hague countries) affixed to the notarial copy; followed by sworn French translation of any non-French supporting annotations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and/or opening attestation of blocked share-capital account (attestation de dépôt de fonds) issued by a French credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French bank, établissement de crédit, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original banker's letter bearing wet signature and bank stamp; no apostille required for domestic French documents; foreign bank letters require apostille/notarization and sworn translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) appointing the French avocat or incorporation agent for signature and filing of the statuts and RCS registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the grantor's country of residence (or French notaire where executed in France)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; any foreign-language instrument must be accompanied by a sworn French translation (traduction assermentée before a French Cour d'appel).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory politically-exposed-person (PEP) assessment of all shareholders, UBOs and the gérant under Articles L.561-10 (2°) and R.561-18 to R.561-18-6 of the Monetary and Financial Code (Decree No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018); systematic negative-media and adverse-information search; screening in real time against the EU consolidated list of persons/entities subject to financial sanctions, the French Direction Générale du Trésor 'assets frozen' list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the US OFAC SDN List, and the FATF/EU high-risk-jurisdiction lists; results documented in an AML file retained per Article L.561-10-2; enhanced due diligence applies to any offshore/trust structure; the client is rated Low_Risk_Standard consistent with ACPR guidelines and must furnish KYC documentation acceptable to Amazon_Pay and Stripe under their respective financial-crime policies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) — sole statutory electronic window for RCS registration (Article 1 of Law No. 2019-486 PACTE); name-availability prior check through the national RCS database published via Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr) and INPI data portal (data.inpi.fr), with complementary EUIPO trademark search.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be expressed in Latin-script characters for inscription in the RCS; foreign-language names are admissible only where romanized/transliterated into the Latin alphabet, and the statutory compulsory particulars — 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL', followed by the share-capital amount and the registered office — must appear in French (Article L.223-1 of the Commercial Code); Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Loi Toubon) governs mandatory French-language drafting of the articles and contractual documents; Chinese-script or Cyrillic-script denominations must adopt an approved romanization and avoid phonetic clashes with existing RCS/NNF registrations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying a regulated banking or credit activity: 'Banque', 'Crédit', 'Caisse', 'Financement', 'Prêt', 'Assurance', 'Mutuelle', 'Caisse d'Épargne' — require prior authorization from the ACPR and/or fall under reserved-sector offences

Regulated professions: 'Avocat', 'Notaire', 'Huissier', 'Médecin', 'Pharmacie', 'Expert-comptable', 'Commissaire aux comptes', 'Architecte' — reserved to title-holders under applicable professional codes

Terms suggesting state sponsorship: 'République', 'National', 'Officiel', 'Président', 'Ministère', 'France' (if used in a manner plausibly implying a public-law link), 'Chambre de commerce', 'Bourse' — require prior ministerial or competent authority approval (R.123-58 Code de commerce and connected régime)

Trade names identical or confusingly similar to a pre-existing RCS entry, a protected trademark (INPI/EUIPO), or a known brand in the toys/preschool sector (e.g., Montessori marks, 'Wooden' toy-family signs) — such conflicts trigger civil and administrative opposition remedies

Any denomination contrary to public order (ordre public) or bonnes mœurs, including misleading product-quality claims regarding eco-certification or child-safety standards, which may also expose the gérant to personal liability under consumer code provisions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a standalone statutory pre-incorporation name-reservation procedure; the 30-day window corresponds to the practitioner-standard currency of an RCS/INPI negative-search certificate applied before the constitutive filing at the Guichet unique. Upon a refus d'immatriculation by the Greffier (including on name-conflict or public-order grounds), the applicant may: (1) within 30 days of notification, file a written réclamation (formal objection/reconsideration request) with the same Greffe under Article R.123-81 of the Commercial Code, annexing corrected articles or an amended denomination; (2) if the Greffier maintains the refusal, petition the President of the Tribunal de commerce by way of référé for an order directing registration, on proof that the legal conditions are met; (3) where the conflict is trademark-based, engage the opposition, transfer or coexistence-negotiation route before INPI/EUIPO and, if necessary, bring an infringement or nullity action before the Tribunal judiciaire; (4) as a preventive measure, re-file the dossier via the Guichet unique with a modified name to preserve the commercial timetable while contested filings are pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered office (siège social) is mandatory for a French SARL. Domiciliation at a specialized commercial domiciliation company or at the residence of the gérant/a director, or at a coworking/business center, is permissible under Articles L.123-11-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code (PACTE Law 2019), subject to the capacity to receive service of process and, for domiciliation companies, registration and statutory disclaimers; for an e-commerce and import-driven toy business using Amazon Fulfillment/Stripe payment rails, the administrative domicile may be a virtual/non-industrial address, but a physical operational site or third-party logistics warehouse in the EU must underpin the inventory supply chain; substance-sensitive checks (tax residence, registration for VAT under Article 209 ff. CGI and the FMC/FAMI duties) require that the génant manager remains reachable at the French seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk — approximately 35% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection in the first 12 months, driven primarily by DGCCRF (French consumer and anti-fraud authority) product-safety controls on toys under Directive 2009/48/EC; about 10% annual probability of a DGFiP (tax administration) physical presence/attestation control on the siège social; under 5% likelihood of Tracfin/ACPR inspection given the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier and low-risk ISIC 3240 classification, provided the UBO file is complete and continuously maintained.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation registration and Greffe redevance payable at the Guichet unique (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via Guichet unique)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory greffe tariff fixed by décret (tarif des greffiers des tribunaux de commerce); approximately EUR 100 for SARL registration including fixed administrative components

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in a legal-announcements gazette (journal d'annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Appointed legal gazette (JAL) of the département of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory maximum regulated by order of the Minister of Finance (prefecture tariff per word/line); prevailing market benchmark EUR 150–200 incl. VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of French-language articles of association (statuts), shareholders' meeting documents, gérant appointment and complete Stage 1 due-diligence file by French avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Avocat registered at the Barreau (e.g., Paris/Essonne) — professional fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed professional fee (honoraires d'avocat) negotiated per dossier; market benchmark EUR 1,000–1,800 for a standard single-member SARL incorporating a foreign corporate shareholder

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille/consular legalization, and sworn French translations of foreign corporate and identity documents (2 apostille sets + 2 certified translations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaries public in country of origin, competent apostille authority (e.g., MOFA/Apostille office), and sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) registered before a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Combined statutory notarial tariffs and apostille rates of the issuing jurisdiction; market benchmark for traduction assermentée approx. EUR 80–140 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Blocked capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de capital) and opening of the French bank account for the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution (bank) or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for the attestation de dépôt de fonds; EUR 25–110 depending on the institution (standard retail tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Annual registered-office domiciliation service at a business/domiciliation center (first-year all-inclusive)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Société de domiciliation (registered commercial domiciliation provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: EUR 250–650 per year depending on the location of the siège social

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance screening report — PEP, sanctions (EU/UN/OFAC/DGT), adverse media, UBO verification and risk rating dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat / independent AML compliance provider engaged for the incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee aligned with ACPR-regulated compliance services; market benchmark EUR 250–450 per UBO dossier

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation, capital, governance and shareholder regime); Articles R.223-1 to R.223-30 (registration and filing formalities); amended by Loi PACTE (2019) and simplified by the 2021 digital administration reforms.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce located in the jurisdiction of the registered office; filings are processed through the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises or the national online portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and transmitted to the INPI National Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (articles of association) signed by all shareholders, accompanied by the incorporation questionnaire Form M0 (or its online functional alternative) and all statutorily required supporting exhibits.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal share capital is imposed for a French SARL; the statutes freely fix the capital that must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be paid up to at least one-fifth (20%) of the subscribed amount upon subscription, the balance payable within five years. The paid-up funds must be deposited with a lawyer, notary, or a prohibited-payment regulated bank account pending registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the shareholders, acting by unanimous consent on this date, do hereby subscribe in full to the registered share capital of five thousand euros (EUR 5,000), divided into five hundred ordinary shares of one euro (EUR 1.00) each, and acknowledge that the statutory minimum paid-up capital requirements have been satisfied. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the company be fixed at 24 Rue de la Forêt, 75011 Paris, France. RESOLVED FURTHER that Mr/Ms [full name], citizen of the Republic, be and hereby is appointed as first manager (gérant) of the SARL for an indefinite term, with all powers to operate, contract, and bind the company, and that he/she accepts the appointment by this writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (notaire) or regulated bank; for the capital deposit, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations also accepts deposits where used.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SARL statutes incorporating mandatory legal clauses: company name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital amount and nominal value, share subscription and payment details, duration, identity and powers of the gérant, distribution rules, and general meeting governance. Open a temporary capital deposit account or escrow arrangement and pay in at least one-fifth of each cash contribution. Obtain the capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds) issued by the financial institution or notary.
required_dossiers: Draft statutes signed by all shareholders
Capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Identity documents of all shareholders and manager
Registered office lease or domiciliation contract
Declaration of no disqualification or bankruptcy (or equivalent standard statement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit certificate is deficient, request correction from the bank or notary. Any legal deficiency in the draft statutes must be remedied by amended draft clauses before execution; a fresh certificate will be issued upon replenishment of the blocked funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of statutes and share subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All shareholders acting together; notary optional but recommended where authenticity of signatures is required for real-property contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the founding shareholders and execute the final statutes in as many originals as necessary for both statutory archives and filing. Each shareholder subscribes to the shares listed in the capital subscription schedule and signs the subscription statement (état de souscription et de versement) inserted in or annexed to the statutes. Confirm the list of initial shareholders and the first gérant appointment clause.
required_dossiers: Final statutes dated and signed by all shareholders
Share subscription and payment statement
Capital deposit certificate
Original or certified copy of registered office lease
Appointment acceptance by the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any shareholder signature is missing, the statutes must be re-executed after obtaining consent; if the share subscription schedule is inconsistent, prepare a rectifying amendment and have all subscribers sign the corrected pages.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal announcement in an approved notices journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An approved legal gazette (Journal d’Annonces Légales) in the department where the registered office is located, chosen by the applicant.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit a concise incorporation announcement (avis de constitution) to the selected JAL containing the exact name, form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, manager identity, and identification of the registry. After verification and payment of publication fee, the JAL issues an attestation de parution (certificate of insertion) necessary for the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Completed JAL announcement form
Name and capital data as written in the statutes
Registered office address
Identity of the gérant
Payment receipt for the legal announcement fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the announcement due to inaccurate data, revise the text and republish immediately. Where the legal publication has already occurred with an error, a corrective insertion must be placed in the same gazette and a new attestation obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation dossier with the Company Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises or the national online portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit electronically or in paper form all incorporation documents: completed Form M0 (in the exact national format), original or electronic version of the signed statutes, capital deposit certificate, registered office justificative, JAL publication certificate, identity documents, manager’s declaration of capacity, and statement of non-bankruptcy. Pay the registry tax and procedural fee upon submission; the central processor then forwards to the competent Greffe and INPI.
required_dossiers: Form M0 (or the online equivalent)
Signed statutes
Capital deposit certificate
Registered office lease or domiciliation agreement
Certificate of legal announcement publication
Identity documents of the gérant
Gérant’s declaration of no disqualification and capacity
Completed declaration of non-bankruptcy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffier issues a query (observation) or request for correction, the applicant must respond within fifteen days by submitting the requested document or amending the electronic file. Failure to correct will result in rejection; a fresh filing fee may be required, so any error must be solved quickly with the support of a legal professional.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of K-Bis certificate and creation of identification numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, in cooperation with the National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI) and the national statistical system (Sirene).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After acceptance of the incorporation file, the Greffe registers the company, generates the K-Bis extract (extrait K-Bis), allocates the SIREN and SIRET numbers, and records the NAF/APE code corresponding to the corporate purpose. The tax and social security administrations are automatically notified, and the applicant can download the official K-Bis to open a corporate bank account and enter into binding agreements.
required_dossiers: No additional application is required once the formation dossier has been approved
Applicant’s procedural reference (Répertoire des Entreprises reference)
Electronic delivery address for receipt of the K-Bis
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-Bis contains an error (name, capital, office, gérant, or APE code), submit a rectification request via the same Greffe service with support from Form M2 or the appropriate formalities portal; rectification is free if requested within legal limits and will be processed as a matter of priority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l’Environnement, de l’Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), particularly the unit responsible for installations classées for environmental protection (ICPE) within the Ministry of Ecological Transition.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d’exploitation au titre de la Rubrique ICPE 2410 « Travail mécanique du bois » (Code de l’environnement, Articles R.512-47 and R.512-54)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l’Environnement, de l’Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) — Inspection des Installations Classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Déclaration « D » (Declaration regime) — a full environmental impact assessment is not required for small artisanal woodworking facilities; the operator must file an environmental pollution declaration and comply with standard sectoral prescriptions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wood dust emissions in the workplace must not exceed 2 mg/m³ over 8 hours (alveolar fraction) with local exhaust ventilation; VOC emissions from varnishes/adhesives must comply with solvent emission thresholds set by the Directive 2004/42/EC; wastewater must not contain hazardous substances above municipal sewer discharge limits; wood waste must be sorted and transferred to licensed valorization or disposal channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Commission Consultative Départementale de la Sécurité et de l’Accessibilité for visited premises; structural load inspection and approved compliance certificate for the building; occupational workplace clearance through the local health and safety inspection unit ensuring conformity with the Labour Code (Articles R.4212-1 et seq.) for ventilation, lighting, personal protective equipment, and machine safety guards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), within the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; centralized business registration via the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent establishing a French SARL must file the incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique (single window operated by INPI) with the statutory declarations (statuts, registered-office lease, proof of manager identity and foreign criminal-record extract, compliance with non-resident ownership rules). Upon registration, the company is issued SIREN/SIRET numbers and the DGFiP automatically allocates the French intra-Community VAT identification number (format: FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN) via the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises. Issuance typically occurs within 1–2 weeks after the company becomes effective (extrait Kbis). The VAT number must be activated in the VIES database; the company must then file the standard VAT status declaration (déclaration de TVA et/ou option fiscale) on impots.gouv.fr and may need to appoint a fiscal representative if it has no French tax domicile for VAT filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box election. A SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level. Statutory elections available: (i) fiscal transparency election for small family SARLs under Article 239 bis AA CGI (all shareholders natural persons, turnover and workforce limits, option valid for five fiscal years under conditions, making profits/losses taxable in shareholders' incomes); (ii) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Articles 256 C III and 286 quater CGI for closely related French entities, with joint and several liability for a renewable five-year period; (iii) fiscal integration (régime de groupe, Art. 223 A CGI) for a French parent holding at least 95% of the SARL for 12 months; and (iv) optional approach to euro-denominated accounting and immediate deduction of certain provisions. Hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD/Art. 212 bis CGI) are mandatory and cannot be elected out of; taxpayers may, however, file binding rulings (rescrit) with DGFiP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold for registration: any taxable person carrying out an independent economic activity in France must register for VAT from the first taxable transaction (Articles 256 et seq. and 286 CGI). The small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA, Art. 293 B CGI) of €91,900 of annual turnover (2024–2025) for the supply of goods, including manufactured wooden toys, relieves the SARL from charging VAT but does not excuse registration; taxable persons making intra-Community acquisitions or exercising the option to tax cannot use the franchise. If turnover exceeds €91,900 (with transitional tolerance up to €113,500), mandatory VAT charging begins from the day of overshoot.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a phased national e-invoicing mandate (réforme de la facturation électronique) for B2B transactions. As of 1 September 2026, all French VAT debtors must receive structured e-invoices through the public portal (Portail Public de Facturation — PPF) or a DGFiP-certified partner platform (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire — PDP); issuance of e-invoices becomes mandatory for large and mid-size enterprises from that date and for all taxable persons (including the SARL) from 1 September 2027. Invoices must be in Factur-X, UBL, or CII formats pursuant to European standard EN 16931; the PDP/PPF performs format and semantic controls (receipt validation) but there is no pre-clearance 'digital stamp' by DGFiP. B2C sales are outside the e-invoicing obligation but require transactional and payment-data e-reporting to the PPF within ten working days after the calendar month end. For intra-Community transactions, e-reporting complements the EC Sales Lists (DEB).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations are zero-rated (véritable exonération with right to deduct input VAT) under Article 262-I-1° CGI, provided the goods physically leave EU customs territory, title and risk pass to the foreign buyer, and the SARL retains the complete proof bundle. Delivery to non-EU Amazon fulfillment centers (US/UK) qualifies as an export only if formally customs-cleared for export from the EU. Intra-Community supplies to a buyer holding a valid EU VAT registration are zero-rated under Article 262 ter CGI subject to issuance of a complete invoice, verification of the buyer's VAT number in VIES, and submission of EC Sales Lists (DEB) within the statutory deadlines; proof of transport must be gathered before the end of the month following the supply (Art. 289 A CGI). Delivery of goods to Amazon French or EU fulfillment centers does not qualify as an export and is domestic/ICV-eligible only with the buyer's VAT ID.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / DAU) lodged via DELTA or GUN-X, identifying the SARL as exporter and the exit customs office from EU territory
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note evidencing physical dispatch and proof of exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of the foreign exchange / payment of the invoice by the non-EU customer
Commercial invoice on company letterhead matching Incoterms, payment terms, and the DAU
Proof of the foreign buyer's non-EU status and delivery acknowledgement/customs seal of the destination territory
For intra-Community zero-rating: buyer's valid EU VAT identification number, EC Sales List (DEB), and transport evidence gathered within the statutory deadline of Article 289 A CGI
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP applies strict documentary enforcement: the statute of limitations for reassessment is three years (Art. L. 176 LPF for VAT), extended up to ten years in cases of fraud or abuse of law (Art. L. 169, L. 64 LPF). Unsubstantiated zero-rating is reclassified as a taxable domestic supply, and the SARL is assessed for outstanding output VAT, late-payment interest (0.20% monthly, Art. 1727 CGI), and penalties equal to 40% (bad faith) or 80% (fraudulent maneuvers) of the rectified sums under Article 1729 CGI. Criminal sanctions for tax fraud apply under Article 1741 CGI: up to 5 years' imprisonment and €500,000 fine, increased to 7 years and €3,000,000 when committed by an organized gang. The gérant (manager) may be held jointly and severally liable for the company's VAT debt (Art. L. 266 LPF); failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days under French foreign exchange rules triggers additional administrative and penal consequences.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem, in coordination with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking supervision and the Direction Générale du Trésor (Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Relance) for foreign-exchange and capital-movement policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full euro convertibility on both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the Code Monétaire et Financier. No exchange-control authorisation is required for dividend distributions, royalty payments, loan repayments, or repatriation of capital to non-resident shareholders. Practical obstacles are limited to anti-money-laundering source-of-funds documentation, balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the Banque de France for transfers exceeding €10,000 (financial relations with foreign countries), and French dividend withholding tax (standard 30% domestic rate, reducible under an applicable double tax treaty where the shareholder is treaty-entitled).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion of export proceeds. Exporters are free to hold foreign currency balances in territorialised foreign-currency accounts (comptes en devises) or convert at market rates through the interbank foreign-exchange market. The only obligation is statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France for individual cross-border transfers or aggregate foreign-exchange relations exceeding the regulatory thresholds (per-transaction/aggregate annual threshold framework under the French foreign-exchange regulations).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) and Operational Current Account (Compte Courant Professionnel)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale (CIC Banque CIC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account (Compte Courant Professionnel) with potential Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary payment flows (Amazon Pay, Stripe payouts, marketplace collections) via an ACPR-licensed French e-money institution or an EEA-passported EMI (e.g., Qonto, Mangopay, Lydia Solutions). Not viable as the authorised repository for statutory capital: EMIs cannot hold a blocked capital account (compte bloqué), cannot provide credit, current-account overdrafts, or documentary credit services, and are not full CRR credit institutions capable of issuing the attestation de blocage required for SARL capital formation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in practice for most Tier-1 banks: the SARL gérant (managing director) must appear physically at a branch or before a notary/delegated officer for initial identification; remote video-identification (visio-identification) is permitted by the ACPR under regulated conditions for French-resident directors with certified providers. Non-resident directors are commonly required to attend a physical KYC interview or deliver notarised and apostilled identity/beneficial-owner packages accompanied by a sworn translation into French. A French registered-office lease (convention de domiciliation) and a KBis extract dated within the last 3 months are unconditional prerequisites.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) opacity or non-resident shareholding chain resembling a shell structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filed at the Tribunal de Commerce; notarised identity documents of every natural person holding 25% or more of capital or voting rights; chain-of-title corporate diagram; foreign UBO tax-residency certificates; sworn French translation of beneficial-owner registrations and criminal-record extracts for each UBO; written narrative explaining the commercial purpose of the non-resident shareholding in the toys manufacturing SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector mismatch underwriting red flag: import of beechwood raw material vs. online retail of finished children's toys
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory business plan with ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930 description of the manufacturing process; pro-forma supplier contracts for FSC-certified beechwood; commercial invoices and Customs declarations (Intrastat and export/import ECS records); product safety and EN-71 conformity documentation for the Montessori blocks; annual transaction-flow projection reconciling raw-material imports with marketplace (Amazon Pay, Stripe) retail settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds for the initial paid-in capital deposited into the blocked account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of original bank statements for every contributing shareholder; certified copy of the deed of contribution in cash (apport en numéraire); bank attestation de blocage certifying the frozen capital deposit; statutory auditors' waiver (abus de droit immédiat) where applicable; signed source-of-wealth declaration confirmed before the compliance officer; copy of the beneficial-owner register extract at deposit date.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade disbursements to higher-risk Asian factor jurisdictions appearing as sporadic SWIFT MT103 operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual procurement budget with counterparty vetting; signed purchase orders and Incoterms schedule; payment against letter of credit (UCP 600) or documentary collection terms; correctly stated EU BOP purpose codes on each wire; set of shipping documents (bill of lading, CMR, freight invoices); appointment of a formal AML/KYC officer (déclaration à l'ACPR) and adoption of an internal compliance manual proving an effective zero-cash, electronic-rails business model.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For Eurozone shareholders, capital injections route via SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer in ISO 20022 XML into the SARL's blocked capital account (compte bloqué) at the French credit institution. For non-EU shareholders, use SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary IBAN and BIC of the blocked account. The payment narrative must state 'Apport en numéraire / Augmentation de capital'; use EU purpose category F05 (direct investment) or standard code DEIN for inward direct investment where an explicit purpose code is mandatory. The bank verifies the transfer against the attestation de blocage and issues the deposit certificate required for the KBis post-filing; no administrative pre-approval is needed, and Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting is handled by the receiving bank for transactions exceeding €10,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Intra-EU supplier settlements (beechwood lumber, packaging, pigments) are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 XML) and SEPA Instant for urgent disbursements; extra-EU payments are cleared via SWIFT MT103 to the beneficiary bank (either a commercial letter of credit under UCP 600 or documentary collection for large consignments), accompanied by commercial invoices, bill of lading/CMR, and Customs export declarations (ECS) to satisfy balance-of-payments statistics. Export proceeds remain freely held in euro or foreign currency; there is no mandatory conversion or surrender. Amazon Pay and Stripe marketplace settlements are onboarded as separate payout rails into the operational euro account, with applicable FX conversion executed at market rates.

permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD forward contracts (change à terme) under MiFID II non-complex OTC derivative treatment
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on non-convertible or exotic currencies where a deliverable forward is impracticable
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for matched asset-liability management of foreign-currency marketplace receivables
FX options on EUR/USD for downside protection of USD retail settlements
Cancelable/rollable foreign-exchange forwards documented under the FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement or ISDA CSAs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS registration confirmation (confirmation annuelle d'inscription)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Infogreffe, Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice (mise en demeure) requiring regularization; persistent failure triggers administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS, loss of separate legal capacity, and personal liability exposure for managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements (dépôt des comptes annuels with balance sheet, income statement and notes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via the RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve accounts within 6 months of FYE; deposit with the Greffe within 1 month of approval, and in all cases no later than 7 months after FYE (31 July for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing exposes the SARL to a monetary fine up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 3,000 for repeat default), court-imposed order to file, and administrative strike-off risk for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration des résultats et de l'IS, Cerfa 2065-SD and related schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December FYE, filed no later than 3 May of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and non-payment attract a 10% penalty on unpaid corporate income tax and late interest of 0.2% per month; intentional omission or tax concealment may escalate the penalty to 40%. No direct strike-off impact, but the tax charge becomes enforceable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local economic contribution declaration (cotisation foncière des entreprises, CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (local tax department)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed by 1 May for calendar-year taxpayers; final CFE payment due by 15 December of the year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the CFE return permits a tax assessment, a EUR 50 per document penalty, plus late interest and a 10% increase for unfiled CFE; unpaid CFE is enforced by treasury distraint and does not affect RCS registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a registered statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when the SARL exceeds at FY-end two of the following three thresholds for the second consecutive year: net turnover (excl. VAT) EUR 8,000,000; balance-sheet total EUR 4,000,000; and average headcount of 50. Other triggers include a shareholder request or court appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) with ANC regulations under the Code de commerce; IFRS permitted only for consolidated financial statements, not for the SARL's individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A standalone annual UBO form is not required; instead the RCS annual confirmation (by 31 March) re-confirms the accuracy of beneficial-owner information recorded on that date. Any transfer of shares or capital notes must be filed within 30 days of the transfer, and the SARL must update the register of beneficial owners within 15 days when the change triggers a new UBO.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of general meetings and manager decisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,200 (EUR 275 - 1,100) per year depending on the domiciliation provider and location
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 25,000 (EUR 2,800 - 23,000) depending on business size, asset structure, and the audit tender; not applicable to an exempt micro-SARL

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) qualifying under Article 219 of the French General Tax Code (CGI) benefit from a reduced corporate income tax rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit per fiscal year, provided the entity's turnover is below EUR 10 million, at least 75% of the share capital is held by individuals, and the paid-in capital is fully liberate. The solidarity surcharge (contribution sociale sur les bénéfices) of 3.3% applies to the portion of corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000, bringing the marginal headline rate to 25.83% for large profits. No statutory tax holiday is available for toy manufacturing; however, the research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) may reduce effective taxation for qualifying product development expenditures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Tax return form CERFA No. 2065 (loyauté et numérique) filed electronically via the professional portal impots.gouv.fr (mode EFI / EDI); supplementary schedules CERFA No. 2052 through 2065-SD as required; separate declaration of digital transactions (Article 299 bis CGI) not applicable to this standard manufacturing scope.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the second working day after May 1st of the fiscal year following the reporting period for fiscal years ending December 31. For non-calendar fiscal years, the return must be filed within three months of the fiscal year-end. Extensions apply for online filing (15 May without penalty for fiscal year-end 31 December). The income tax return serves as the definitive self-assessment; the first instalment of corporate income tax for the following year is due on 15 March.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit or deficit after deduction of allowable expenses and application of the 15% reduced rate threshold on the first EUR 42,000 of profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL is taxable on France-source profits; apportionment must be supported by a permanent establishment analysis and transfer pricing documentation. Enter France-sourced taxable income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains and losses on disposal of fixed assets, including industrial equipment used in beechwood processing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report disposition of French situs assets including goodwill, client portfolios, and leasehold rights. Rate of taxation may be 25% or reduced rates under Article 219 CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director remuneration, employee wages, and associated social security charges (cotisations sociales) deductible from taxable profit if incurred for the French business and duly substantiated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Manager (gérant) remuneration for foreign resident directors must be supported by time allocation and substance evidence; excessive payments may be reclassified as non-deductible distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax credits including CIR, CII, and family tax credit (crédit d'impôt famille) where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit eligibility is limited to French establishment activities; claim only qualifying R&D and innovation expenditures attributable to the French PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of VAT returns and payment status for the fiscal year; failure to attach appropriate CA12 or CA3 declarations triggers rejection.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL must hold a French VAT number for any French supplies; intra-EU distance selling thresholds must be monitored.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge of the assessed tax. Repeated failure within 30 days after formal notice: 40%. Intentional concealment or abusive filing: 80%. Monthly late payment interest (intérêt de retard) of 0.20% per month from the statutory due date. Automatic penalty of EUR 150 per missing supporting schedule. Failure to file the transfer pricing documentation: EUR 5,000 per document, or 5% of the value of the undocumented related-party transactions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (12.8% withholding tax under the single flat tax / prélèvement for individuals, plus 17.2% social levies; 25% for corporate entities receiving dividends from a French SARL unless treaty relief is available).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the reduced rate under the France–China DTA (or any applicable treaty), the dividend beneficiary must submit to the French paying entity a certification of tax residence (Formulaire 2766-SD) before the date of dividend payment and provide the foreign tax residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) issued by the Chinese tax authority, endorsed under Article 29 of the treaty. The paying entity submits the annual recapitulative statement (Déclaration 2561) with supporting certificates to the local tax office (SIE). Where no treaty claim is filed in time, the 30% statutory withholding is applied and the excess must be reclaimed through the non-resident refund procedure (réclamation contentieuse) within the framework of the EU Interest & Royalties Directive or applicable DTA arbitration/MAP procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory gross withholding 33.33% (Article 182 B CGI); treaty-reduced to 10% under the France–China DTA, and 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive if the beneficial owner is an EU associated company. Interest: statutory withholding 30% (Article 119 bis 2 CGI); treaty-reduced to 10% under most DTAs; exemption under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive where the 25% shareholding test is met. Forholding analysis must verify anti-abuse provisions (principal purpose test) under Article 13 of the DTA and French GAAR (Article 205 A CGI).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million consolidated group turnover threshold mandates Master File; Local File documentation and transfer pricing declaration (Formulaire 2257-SD) are mandatory for any French entity with related-party transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 in aggregate per fiscal year, regardless of group size. For the subject SARL, documentation is required if intercompany purchases of timber, sales of finished toys, or IP charges exceed EUR 50,000 annually, or if the entity operates in a jurisdiction listed as non-cooperative.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the economic substance doctrine through the anti-abuse rules of Article 155 A CGI (services rendered by non-residents), Article 119 bis 2, and the abuse of law procedure (abus de droit) under Article L64 of the Livre des procédures fiscales. For EU-based intermediary or shell entities, the ATAD 1 anti-hybrid rules and the EU substance requirements (DAC 6 hallmark C.1) are incorporated in CGI Articles 209 B and 205 A; a French-relevant shell entity with no local employees, premises, or commercial activity in an NFT context will be deemed to lack substance, and the tax administration may recharacterise all profit repatriation as French-source taxable income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of French taxable profit, concealment of turnover, use of fictitious suppliers for beechwood raw material, or invoicing foreign related parties below cost to shift margin out of France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of five years (Article 1741 CGI); tax reassessment with 80% penalty (Article 1729 CGI) plus 0.20% monthly interest and publication of the penalty decision. Sanctions may be doubled where proceeds laundered or organised group involvement is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be jointly and severally liable for company tax debt upon a finding of serious or repeated misconduct (Article L267 LPF); criminal conviction triggers individual asset seizure, travel bans, and a five-year imprisonment term; professional ban under Article 1742 CGI and European arrest warrant risk for non-cooperation with judicial proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulation of the wholesale price of wooden toy blocks to an Asian or EU parent at a below-cost margin, or payment of excessive royalties for a simple trademark licence without active substance in France, avoiding the arm's length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the transfer price under Article 57 CGI; 40% bad faith penalty or 80% for abusive manipulation; EUR 5,000 penalty per missing TP document; potential permanent establishment recharacterisation of the non-resident parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally participate in profit shifting face personal liability under Article L266 LPF for unpaid corporate tax when they have caused the company's deficiency; criminal referral may impose personal fines not covered by the company and extradition risk under mutual legal assistance agreements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Shell Entity / Absence of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishment of a French SARL without premises, employees, or operational autonomy, merely channelling toy sales to avoid VAT or corporate tax in the parent jurisdiction; failure to comply with French substance expectations; invocation of treaty benefits without genuine activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rebutting of tax residence or denial of treaty benefits through the principal purpose test; re-attribution to the parent's French PE; 80% penalty on the undisclosed tax base under Article 1729 CGI; DAC 6 disclosure penalties of EUR 10,000 per scheme, and EUR 50,000 for intentional failure to disclose cross-border arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell identified under ATAD 1 are jointly liable for the re-attributed taxes under Article L267 LPF; civil liability on grounds of artificial legal arrangement, travel restrictions imposed by the judicial authorities, and up to three years for false declarations under Article 441-1 French Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the toy sales legal entity to receive funds without KYC or source verification from third parties, passing off structured payments as franchise fees, or clearing toy sale proceeds through personal wallets/mules to conceal tax fraud or ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code, Article 465-1 provides a five-year prison term and EUR 375,000 fine for money laundering; aggravated money laundering raises penalties to ten years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 fine; TRACFIN investigation and asset confiscation orders apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners face personal criminal exposure independent from the SARL shield; confiscation of personal assets, bank account freezes, travel bans and prohibition to manage a business; non-compliant compliance officers face a EUR 10,000 fine and two years' imprisonment for failure to report suspicious transactions to TRACFIN.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Violation of Profit Repatriation Rules / Withholding Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorrect application of the zero or reduced withholding resulting from a falsified tax residence certificate, or distributing dividends disguised as management fees to avoid the 30% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Requalification of fees as dividends with assessment of 30% withholding, 40% or 80% penalty, plus legal interest; the beneficiary is not entitled to a foreign tax credit in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to pay the withheld tax personally if they knowingly structured the distribution without withholding payment (Article L266 LPF) and face criminal fines for misrepresentation under Article 433-4 Criminal Code (of forged administration documents) up to three years' imprisonment.
